title: Reduced Quantum-Reference-Frame Channels for Open Quantum Systems
authors: Paolo Luppi, Viktoria Kabel, Flaminia Giacomini, Andrea Smirne
abstract: When reference frames are treated quantum mechanically, the subsystem structure of quantum systems is no longer absolute, but depends on the choice of the quantum reference frame (QRF). This raises a basic question: which dynamical properties are preserved across QRFs, and which depend on the physical reference used to define the system? We study this question in the general setting of open quantum systems. At the operational level, after a QRF transformation, the old reference frame and environmental degrees of freedom may be inaccessible and must therefore be traced out. This motivates the definition of reduced quantum-reference-frame channels: maps that connect the joint description in one frame to the accessible subsystem in another. We characterize their symmetry-constrained structure and define a regime in which a reduced entropy-coherence conservation law holds. We also identify when the induced reduced action on the open system admits a classical interpretation as random frame misalignment, and when it instead reflects quantum reduced-frame effects. We then apply the framework to pure-dephasing dynamics and derive a necessary and sufficient compatibility condition for population preservation. When the frame symmetry commutes with the open system's free Hamiltonian, coherences acquire a multiplicative frame factor, so that locally inferred decoherence rates split into environmental and reference-induced contributions. Ramsey interferometry gives this split a direct operational meaning. Finally, a gravity-motivated dephasing model illustrates how degradation of a phase reference can mimic signatures usually attributed to intrinsic decoherence mechanisms.
summary: This paper develops a theory for describing open quantum systems when viewed from different Quantum Reference Frames (QRFs). It introduces 'reduced QRF channels' to account for inaccessible degrees of freedom. The key finding is that decoherence rates can be mathematically split into contributions arising separately from the environment and the reference frame itself.
main_problem: The paper investigates which dynamical properties of open quantum systems remain invariant when viewed from a different Quantum Reference Frame (QRF). It addresses the fundamental question of subsystem relativity in quantum dynamics.
main_result: It derives reduced quantum-reference-frame channels and shows that decoherence rates can split into distinct environmental and reference-induced contributions, which is operationally testable via Ramsey interferometry.
method: The analysis employs a formal framework involving QRF transformations, partial tracing over inaccessible degrees of freedom (environment/reference frame), and characterizing the resulting reduced quantum channels.
model_or_system: The study models open quantum systems interacting with an environment, extending to include reference frames. Specific applications include pure-dephasing dynamics and a gravity-motivated dephasing model.
key_observables: Reduced entropy conservation law, decoherence rates (split into environmental and reference-induced parts), population preservation conditions, and Ramsey visibility.
important_parameters: The structure of the QRF symmetry representation; the nature of the coupling between system, environment, and reference frame.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the perspectival approach to QRFs and assumes that only operationally accessible degrees of freedom are retained after tracing out inaccessible ones.
figures_summary: Figure 5 illustrates a Ramsey interferometer protocol implemented on an effective qubit subspace, showing how outcome probabilities and decoherence rates can be calculated in different reference frames.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general framework for QRF transformations in open systems. It then characterizes the reduced channels, derives conservation laws, applies these concepts to pure dephasing dynamics (showing rate splitting), and concludes with an illustration using a gravity-motivated model.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding how environmental coupling and measurement context (the reference frame) fundamentally alter the perceived dynamics of quantum systems, which has implications for quantum sensing and gravity.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Block preservation. A block population p(B) n in frame B may receive contributions from different blocks m of S in frame A, with the dependence on inaccessible degrees of freedom encoded in the effects Πnm. Inter-block coherences of S in frame A do not contribute to these populations. A one-to-one permutation correspondence between input and output blocks gives the stronger condition of strong block-preservation. Edges are illustrative.

Figure 2: Same physical interferometer. Alice performs a Ramsey experiment M (A) on system S. Bob has access to A’s phase record and outcomes and describes the same physical interferometer from his point of view. The operational Ramsey visibility (and the associated rate) is frame-invariant: γ(B | access A) nm = γ(A) nm. The shadowed images represent possible superpositions of relative configurations between the systems and the reference frame.

Figure 3: Local Ramsey (different phase standards). Observers Alice and Bob perform Ramsey experiments M (A) resp. M (B) using their own phase references A and B. The inferred decoherence rates can differ. In the Hamiltonian-symmetric regime, the difference is captured by a frame factor, i.e. VB(t) = |Fnm(t)| VA(t).

Figure 4: Reference-induced contributions to the locally inferred decoherence rate in the gravity-motivated pure- dephasing case study. Left: for linear phase-reference degradation, σ2 θ(t) = ΓBt, the reference adds a constant contribution γfr 01 = ΓB/2, so that γ(B) 01 = γ(A) 01 + γfr 01. Right: for ballistic phase spreading, σ2 θ(t) = κBt2, the reference-induced contribution is time dependent, γfr 01(t) = κBt, and the inferred rate grows with both time and the instability parameter κB.

Figure 5: Ramsey protocol on the effective qubit {|n⟩, |m⟩} (σ(nm) z = |n⟩⟨n| −|m⟩⟨m|). The pulses U1, U2(φ) and the free evolution Ufree,SE(t) map the coherence ρnm onto a measurable population imbalance; the transverse Bloch-vector length equals the Ramsey visibility Vnm = 2|ρnm|, from which the decoherence rate is obtained.
